title: Overnight Sausage Strata
subtitle: Make-ahead bread, sausage, and egg bake rested overnight and baked hot.
description: Sausage, bread, and cheese layered overnight with egg custard, baked until puffed and golden. Make-ahead hall breakfast for early shift change.

ingredients.name: dry mustard
ingredients.notes: plus salt, pepper, and pinch nutmeg

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: plus hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Overnight Sausage Strata in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Brown sausage and build layers
steps.instruction: Cook sausage until no pink remains and internal temperature reaches 160°F; drain. Grease a deep 9x13 pan. Layer half the bread cubes, sausage, optional onion, and half the cheddar. Repeat layers.

steps.title: Mix and pour custard
steps.instruction: Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, salt, pepper, and nutmeg until smooth. Pour evenly over the bread layers, pressing gently so all cubes contact liquid.

steps.title: Refrigerate overnight
steps.instruction: Cover tightly and refrigerate at least 8 hours or overnight so bread fully absorbs custard. Remove from fridge 30 minutes before baking to take the chill off the pan.

steps.title: Bake until puffed
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Top with remaining cheddar. Bake uncovered 45–50 minutes until center reaches 165°F, top is golden, and a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Overnight Sausage Strata onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 10 minutes before cutting into squares so custard sets for clean portions. Garnish with green onions and serve with hot sauce at the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Overnight Sausage Strata — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Assemble the night before so morning service is mostly oven time.
Use stale bread—fresh bread turns to mush after an overnight soak.
Check center temp with a probe; golden top can hide under-set custard in the middle.
cleanupNotes: Wash the assembly pan the morning of service while the strata bakes in the oven.
Discard any custard that spilled and baked onto the oven floor once cooled.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Cube leftovers and pan-fry in butter for crispy strata hash with a fried egg on top.
